newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's IEB bank to expand in E.Europe.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's IEB bank to expand in E.Europe.

text.p: Hungary's Inter-Europa Bank (IEB), controlled by Italy's San Paolo di Bancario group, plans the expansion of its network in Hungary and central and eastern Europe, the bank said on Friday.
The plans include opening a new office in Ukraine soon.
"From 1997 on, the bank begins preparations for appearing on the central and eastern European markets," IEB said in a statement in the Budapest Stock Exchange's official gazette.

"In this new role, Inter-Europa is planned to become an associated member of the San Paolo group, and for the longer-term, the representative of the business interests of the group in this region," it said.
IEB had good results in 1996, posting a pre-tax profit of more than two billion forints on a balance sheet total of about 91 billion forints, the bank said.
Its 1996 pre-tax profit was around the targeted 2.25 billion forints, while its balance sheet total well exceeded the planned 9.3 billion forint.
IEB said earlier that tough competition on the Hungarian banking market had compelled it to change its strategy during 1996 and boost its balance sheet total.
Being the first Hungarian joint venture bank to recognise the importance of developing its on-line connected branch network was the basis of good results in 1996, IEB said.
The bank has 15 branches and representative offices, and plans for expansion mainly aim at adding new representative offices, controlled by existing branches.
As the first step, an IEB representative office near the Zahony border crossing to Ukraine will be opened on January 20.
The bank also expects the Ukraine banking watchdog to authorise it in January to open a representative office in Kiev in March.
"Among Hungary's eastern neighbours, the second largest country of Europe, Ukraine, involves enormous but so far unexploited business opportunities," IEB said.
